questions.q: The Robinson annulation consists of which two reactions, in order?
options: Michael addition, then intramolecular aldol condensation
questions.explain: A ketone enolate first adds 1,4 to methyl vinyl ketone, and the resulting 1,5-diketone then cyclises by an intramolecular aldol condensation.

questions.q: The intermediate isolated after the Michael step between cyclohexanone and methyl vinyl ketone is:
questions.explain: The enolate attacks the β-CH₂ of CH₂=CH–CO–CH₃, attaching a –CH₂CH₂COCH₃ (3-oxobutyl) chain to give a 1,5-diketone.

questions.q: 2-Methylcyclohexane-1,3-dione undergoes Robinson annulation with methyl vinyl ketone. The product is:
questions.explain: This bicyclic enedione is the Wieland–Miescher ketone, a classic steroid building block; Δ¹,⁹-octal-2-one comes from plain cyclohexanone.

questions.q: Why does the intramolecular aldol step of the Robinson annulation close a six-membered ring?
options: The ring C=O attacks the side-chain C=O directly
The Michael adduct is a 1,5-diketone, and the terminal CH₃ enolate attacks the ring C=O to form a strain-free six-membered ring
Methyl vinyl ketone supplies six carbons to the new ring
questions.explain: 1,5-Diketones cyclise to cyclohexenones. MVK supplies only four carbons; the other two come from the C=O and α-carbon of the original ketone.
